current.text: He is a projected starter for the Warriors.
He is unlikely to play much center because he is old and small. The more he does play center, the more minutes open up for Santos and Lendeborg.
One expert sees him outside the top 120 in category leagues because of his age and because he fades when Curry sits. That makes his Yahoo ADP of 107 too high.
He is good value as a late pick in deep leagues, around pick 176 to 181. The experts would not take him in round 13 of a 12-team league or in a 10-team league.
One center ranking puts him in tier nine, and that expert is souring on him more every day.
The Warriors are reportedly treating this season as a gap year.
The team may rest veterans to protect its lottery odds. Experts expect Warriors players to fade as the season goes on.
The Warriors have 15 back-to-backs, tied for second most in the league.
The Warriors' schedule is good for fantasy playoffs that end on March 28.
The Warriors' depth is very poor, so minutes should go up across the rotation.

durable.text: He is better in category leagues than in points leagues.
He gives rebounds and assists, but his steals and blocks have fallen.
His assists are guard-like for a forward or center. This is his clearest category strength.

note: He ranks 152 on Yahoo and 163 on ESPN, and both sites value him at 0 USD. That puts him just outside the 144 players we draft, so he is a 1 USD final pick at most (our league paid 4 USD last season) or a waiver option. His value is mostly assists from a frontcourt slot (5.5 projected, with a small steals edge). It comes with weak points, turnovers (2.5) and FG% (43%), so he only suits builds that need frontcourt assists and can absorb the turnovers. Early in the season, check whether he gets center minutes, whether his steals and blocks come back, and whether the Warriors start resting veterans as the gap year goes on.
